messages.subject: Call for testing upcoming RKWard 0.7.5
messages.body_plain:
Hi!

It is once again time to bring the changes in the RKWard development
tree to a wider audience. A release on October 25 seems doable:
https://rkward.kde.org/Release_Schedule.html .

Of course, as usual, I'm hoping for your help in testing, to make sure
the final release does not suffer from avoidable defects.

As for what to look out for, many changes concern the following areas:

- Many new code snippets have been added, and existing snippets have
  been improved.
- There is a new option to restart the R backend. This can be very
  useful when trying to make sure that a script is fully reproducible.
- Code completions have been improved. Among other things help topics
  ("?xyz"), and objects inside packages that are not currently loaded
  ("package:::xyz") can be completed. 

Looking forward to your feedback!
Thomas

messages.subject: install rkward in Linux Slackware 15
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

On Mon, 10 Oct 2022 22:20:25 +1300
Fabian Labra-Sprohnle <flabra at xtra.co.nz> wrote:
> I wonder if someone of you has been able to install rkward in*Linux 
> Slackware 15*. I would appreciate any help to do that

The generic starting point would be
https://rkward.kde.org/Building_RKWard_From_Source.html, if you get
stuck, post the specific error message, and we can likely talk you
through the process.

Alternatively, there is usable AppImage for the upcoming release at
https://binary-factory.kde.org/view/AppImage/job/RKWard_Nightly_appimage-centos7/
, which should work on any Linux distribution (all you have to do is
mark the downloaded package as executable).

Regards
Thomas
